overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: its minutes response was compliant and deliberation was unsupported. Complaints against the assessor and clerk were declined as non-members and untimely.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to produce minutes in response to his June 2 request for Board minutes about 138 Ayer Road.
allegations.key_passage: We find, therefore, that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law in response to the complainant’s request for minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to produce site visit documentation and correspondence about 138 Ayer Road in response to his request.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent that the complainant alleges that the Board failed to produce site visit documentation and correspondence, that allegation falls outside the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Board members discussed and deliberated on his property (138 Ayer Road) by communicating outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board did not deliberate outside a meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints filed with the Principal Assessor and Town Clerk alleged Open Meeting Law violations by municipal employees, who are not Board members.
allegations.key_passage: Both Principal Assessor Wilson and Clerk Oelfke are municipal employees, not members of the Board.

allegations.summary: Complaints against the Principal Assessor and Town Clerk, alleging violations on May 20, May 22 and June 3, were filed with the AG more than 90 days later.
Complaints also raised property classification, inspection demands, and civil rights, due process and tortious interference claims.
allegations.key_passage: All of these allegations fall outside the Open Meeting Law.
